mappings.note: Shared features read as evidence of common ancestry -- C4.5's 'evidences of biological evolution'. Not C-4.1-LO-1: the features are not being used to sort organisms into groups here, they are being read as descent. C4.5 carries no learning outcomes of its own, so it is cited at competency level.

Organelles doing inside one cell what organs do in a body: the C4.2 competency, 'levels of organisations of living organisms (from molecules to organisms)', is the only row covering that. Not C-4.1-LO-1, which uses cell number as a sorting criterion -- nothing is being sorted here, the ask is how one cell suffices.

Bryophyte body differentiation -- rhizoids and leaf-like structures, no vascular tissue. Plant divisions have NO learning outcome in this curriculum (C4.2-LO-5..LO-8 are all animal-specific), so the whole plant-group family sits on the C4.2 competency. Not C-4.1-LO-2: the kingdom is not in question, the division inside Plantae is.

Xylem and phloem as the tissue level serving a tall body -- C4.2's levels of organisation. Shares the plant-division family's single home. Not C4.5: no evolutionary advantage is argued, only the transport requirement that height imposes.

Seeds and fruits as adaptations that widen where a plant can live -- C4.5's 'changes in structure, and function of organisms'. Not C4.2: no level of body organisation is traced; the payload is protection, stored food and dispersal, that is, adaptive advantage.

Both phyla are handed over in the stem; what is probed is the survival value of the exoskeleton, so C4.5 (structure and function) and not C4.2-LO-5, which places an animal in its phylum from the level of organisation reached. Not C4.2-LO-7 either: segmentation is the shared background here, not the discriminator. Arthropoda has no outcome of its own.

Whether biodiversity means species alone or also habitats, ecosystems and genetic variety -- the biosphere and its interrelationships, C2.8. Not C5.2: no conservation choice or human impact is asked. Not LO-15: no interaction between two groups of organisms is analysed.

Lists what to OBSERVE -- prokaryote or eukaryote, unicellular or multicellular, cell wall, mode of nutrition -- which is C-4.1-LO-1 almost word for word. Not C-4.1-LO-2: no kingdom is actually assigned, the pond organism stays unnamed.

DNA comparison as evidence of true evolutionary relationship is C4.5; it is presented as the modern method that sees what morphology cannot, which is C7.1's 'most current understanding of the matter being studied'. Not C-4.1-LO-1: genetic similarity is not among its named characteristics and no organism is sorted.

Climate altering the conditions species are adapted to -- C2.8's interconnected Earth systems and hazards. Not C5.2: the item stops at the mechanism and never reaches a conservation case study. Not C4.5: no inherited change or selection is claimed, only habitat becoming unsuitable.

Jointed legs place the animal in Arthropoda rather than Annelida -- LO-5's 'uses the level reached to place an animal in its phylum', which is this curriculum's only phylum-placement row. Not C4.2-LO-7: segmentation is the distractor here, the feature that fails to separate insect from earthworm.

The answer turns on one cell-level characteristic -- membrane present, cell wall absent -- used to place the sponge in Animalia, which is C-4.1-LO-1. Not C4.2-LO-6: Porifera's lack of true tissues is given in the stem as background, and the question is a kingdom discriminator, not a Porifera/Cnidaria contrast.

Two asks in one item: which features distinguish the two animals (C-4.1-LO-1) and how those features place them into groups -- the worked answer resolves to bird against earthworm, that is, phylum placement from body plan (C4.2-LO-5). Not C-4.1-LO-2: no kingdom is named.

Justifies WHY cellular organisation outranks vascular tissue as a criterion -- LO-9's 'how levels of cellular and body organisation guided the move to a five-kingdom classification'. Not C-4.1-LO-1, which applies the criterion; this item argues for choosing it in the first place.
A nucleus plus a single cell yields a kingdom: Protista. C-4.1-LO-2 is the placement row. Not C-4.1-LO-1: the characteristics are supplied by the slide description, the work is the assignment.

Producers, consumers and decomposers holding the system steady: LO-15 is 'interactions between members of different groups of organisms' and C2.8 the system-level stability that results. Not C5.2 -- no conservation decision or human impact is in play.

Prokaryotes and eukaryotes forced into one box is precisely the failure that pushed classification past its earlier kingdoms -- LO-9. Not C-4.1-LO-2, which sorts organisms using the system; this item examines the system itself.

Viruses fail the cellular-organisation criterion the five kingdoms are built on -- LO-9. Held to this one code: unlike the two items after it, this one asks only why viruses are excluded and never generalises to how classification changes.

The ask is a judgement about the SYSTEM and what revising it shows -- C7.1, current and revisable understanding -- resting on the cellular criterion of LO-9. Not CG7: C7.1 is the competency under that goal and is the more precise row.

Same pair as the item before it, and stated honestly: the two questions approach one thing from opposite ends (propose a revision / name the limitation) and curriculum 82 has exactly one home for each half. No distinction invented.

Bryophyte against pteridophyte, separated on body differentiation and vascular tissue -- levels of body organisation, C4.2. Third member of the plant-division family sharing this competency because no plant-division outcome exists in this curriculum.

POOR FIT, and a gap worth recording: the seven-rank taxonomic hierarchy (class against genus) has NO outcome in curriculum 82 for this chapter. C-4.1-LO-2 is cited only for its opening clause 'Classify various organisms in groups'; its stated basis -- cellular organisation and ecological role -- has nothing to do with rank depth.

The point is which characters DECIDE: locomotion and autotrophy do not, unicellular-plus-eukaryotic does. That is C-4.1-LO-1's 'number of cells present, cellular organisation'. Not C-4.1-LO-2, which would be the plain name-the-kingdom item this one deliberately refuses to be.

Asks for the identification key -- chitin wall and absorptive heterotrophy -- so the mode-of-nutrition clause of C-4.1-LO-1. Same row as the Protista-key item above, because both probe the discriminating characteristic rather than the kingdom it yields.

A feature table resolved into Monera, Fungi and Protista, including R's autotroph-or-heterotroph switch: C-4.1-LO-2 names both 'cellular organisation' and 'ecological role'. Not C-4.1-LO-1: the characteristics arrive ready-made in the table, the work is the placement.
